idiom_name: SQLAlchemy Core select() expressions (or Django Q objects)
implementation_notes: Python's query object is library-provided: SQLAlchemy Core's select(cols).where(...).join(...) returns a new Select for each composition (GenerativeSelect), compiled per dialect with bound parameters at execution, and Django's Q objects are the same idea with &, | and ~ overloaded on predicate objects passed to QuerySet.filter. What replaces the classic query class in both is a library expression object that can be stored, passed and compiled; a hand-rolled predicate class over raw DB-API/sqlite3 stays justified for small scripts where an expression layer is unwarranted.
code_sketch:
stmt = select(customer.c.id, customer.c.name).where(customer.c.status == "active")
if min_age is not None:
    stmt = stmt.where(customer.c.age >= min_age)   # new Select; the old one is untouched
stmt = stmt.order_by(customer.c.name).limit(50)
rows = conn.execute(stmt).mappings().all()
pitfalls: Textual fragments (text(), f-strings) bypass parameter binding and reopen injection while defeating dialect compilation caches.
Django Q trees do not compose like chained filters: Q(a) | Q(b) inside one filter is not two .filter() calls (which AND), and a sliced queryset cannot be filtered further.
Statements are immutable but their MetaData is not: rebuilding a Table against a changed schema invalidates cached compiled SQL.
